disclosure: Every transcript below is synthetic. No real Slack message, real person, or private team discussion appears in this file.

transcripts.name: premature_auth_consensus
transcripts.note: Two teammates close on self-hosted authentication without naming an owner for session revocation or the on-call cost.

messages.text: The identity vendor bill doubled again for next quarter.
Then lets just self-host auth. The library does most of it already.
Agreed. Two weeks of work at most and we own the whole flow.
I can start the service on Monday and cut the vendor before renewal.
Do it. I will tell finance we are dropping the contract.
Locked in. Moving it to the sprint board now.

transcripts.name: healthy_auth_decision
transcripts.note: The same decision, but ownership, session revocation, rollback, and on-call are all addressed in the thread.

messages.text: Proposal: move auth in house before the renewal date.
Who owns password reset, session revocation, and the pager for it?
I own the service and I am on the rotation. Revocation is in the design doc with a forced logout test.
Rollback plan? Last migration hurt because we could not go back.
We keep the vendor live in parallel for 30 days and can flip back in one config change.
That covers the cost and the exit. Approved for the next sprint.

transcripts.name: irrelevant_memory
transcripts.note: A low-risk naming choice closes quickly. No memory record is analogous, so precedent must not be invented.

messages.text: Do we call the settings tab Preferences or Settings?
Settings. It matches the mobile app already.
Fine by me, it is a one line copy change.
Settings it is. Merging the copy update.
